key_insight: Pressure can be treated as a geometric field that curves an effective spatial metric, making pressure-driven motion equivalent to geodesic flow and linking vortex criteria to curvature invariants.
engineering_relevance: This offers a unified geometric framework for interpreting turbulence diagnostics and could improve the physical consistency of vortex identification in CFD and flow analysis.
method: Build a Newton-Cartan geometric formulation of fluid flow.
Apply a conformal transformation to map pressure into effective spatial curvature.
Relate vortex identification criteria to Eulerian/Lagrangian geometric invariants and curvature projections.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical derivation, including recovery of the Euler equation in the weak-field limit and consistency with the pressure Poisson equation and Bianchi identity, rather than a data-driven benchmark.
watch_item: The framework is highly theoretical and may be difficult to validate or apply robustly in noisy experimental or high-Reynolds-number simulation data.
paper_title: On the relationships between pressure geometrization and vortex identification
